about.title: Fontana Car Accident Claims
about.longDescription: Fontana sits where the I-10 San Bernardino Freeway meets a grid of wide surface streets, and that mix shows up in the collision record. In 2025, the city logged 799 injury collisions, with 1,105 people hurt and 21 lives lost. Public counts run highest along Sierra Avenue, Citrus Avenue, Foothill Boulevard, and the I-10 corridor, and reports cluster on Friday afternoons between 3 and 5 p.m., when the end-of-week commute is building. If you were injured in one of these crashes, the days right after matter. Photos, witness names, medical records, and the other driver's insurance information are easier to gather now than later. LawProactive is not a law firm. We are a free service that connects Fontana residents with an independent personal injury attorney who handles car accident claims in San Bernardino County. That attorney works on contingency, so you owe no fee unless there is a recovery. You describe what happened; we make the connection; the attorney takes it from there.

items.title: The clock is real in California
items.desc: Most car accident claims must be filed within two years, but if a city, county, or Caltrans vehicle was involved, the window can shrink to six months. Getting connected early keeps those deadlines from sneaking up on you.

items.title: Being partly at fault does not end your claim
items.desc: California follows pure comparative fault, meaning your recovery is reduced by your share of blame rather than erased. An attorney can push back when an insurer tries to pin more of the crash on you than the evidence supports.

items.title: No fee unless there is a recovery
items.desc: Attorneys in our network work on contingency, and our connection service costs you nothing. California also places no cap on non-economic damages like pain and suffering in ordinary car accident cases.

items.question: The other driver's insurance company called and wants a recorded statement. Should I give one?
items.answer: You are not required to give a recorded statement to the other driver's insurer, and it is generally wise to hold off until you have spoken with an attorney. Adjusters may use casual remarks to argue you were more at fault than you were. Report the crash to your own carrier as your policy requires, but let counsel handle the other side.

items.question: I was hit near the I-10 and Sierra Avenue interchange in Fontana. Does it matter where the crash happened?
items.answer: Location can matter in a few ways. Crashes on or near the freeway often involve the CHP rather than Fontana Police, which affects where you request the report. If a public agency's vehicle or a roadway condition played a role, a much shorter six-month government claim deadline may apply, so mention the exact spot when you reach out.

items.question: What should I keep or gather before I talk to an attorney?
items.answer: Save everything: photos of the vehicles and scene, the exchange of information, the police report number, and any medical paperwork or receipts. Write down what you remember while it is fresh, including the time of day and weather. If a nearby business might have camera footage, note its name so it can be requested before it is overwritten.
